title: kbsettings reads five layers, defaults, group, clone, kb root and user, lets a group lock a key, and explain names the layer and file that decided each one
goal: kbsettings.effective merges the defaults, the group file, the clone file, the kb root file and the user file in that order, later over earlier; the group file is the file group_settings names in the clone's settings.json; KB_GROUP_SETTINGS names the group file when the clone names none; the clone file is <WS>/settings.json, or <WS>/.it-ops-kb/settings.json when that file exists as in a host project with the plugin installed; the kb root file is <WS>/kb/<root>/settings.json when --kb-root names the root; the user file <WS>/_private/settings.json wins over every other layer; kbsettings.layered(root, name, kb_root) returns the top-level object name merged over the same layers with a map from each key to its layer, for extensions, extension_paths, backlog, gate_checks, group and leak; a key a group file lists under locked raises SettingsError naming the key and the group file when a later layer sets it, exit 2; explain prints each key's source as default, group, clone, root or user with the file
